instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You offered to finish the fete banner. I copied your big SAMPLE heading to get it started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was the printer's proof. SAMPLE isn't part of the banner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a test heading. Replace it with RAFFLE and put the draw time underneath.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can paint a time, but nobody has organized the draw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the unfinished bit of the banner you offered to finish. Arrange the draw, then you can fill in its time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stamped the wedding envelopes like you showed me. You said you'd help get them posted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those are address labels, not stamps. I offered to show you where the post office is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, addresses first. You'll know which postage comes next.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll meet you at the post office at nine. Bring the envelopes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring them to you at nine, then. You can take them to the counter and finish the help you offered.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you help clear out the committee cupboard? I've crossed off names just as you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, but my crosses mark who missed the meeting. They don't mean throw out their files.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, attendance first. Let's clear out the members who never turn up, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered to sort paper. My name's crossed out too; I was in hospital.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me separate an absence from an excuse. We'll keep your file and start asking the others where they were.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I signed where you signed. Now help me save the club garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gladly, but I signed the extension plan. It builds over half the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, getting inside the proposal. We'll start by withdrawing both our signatures.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for the planning drawings myself. I don't want that money wasted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me find a use for those drawings that keeps the garden. You're joining the redesign, not the building campaign.

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've locked both our bags away, just like the instructor. Leave them there while we discuss the climbing wall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She was testing a broken lock. You've put our bags in a locker we can't open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, equipment checked. Ask her to release them after the safety talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can wait through a safety talk. I'm not agreeing to climb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. With the bags dealt with, put a harness on for the talk. Then you'll already be ready when they ask who wants a turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed Saturday on the hall calendar like you. Let's leave it marked while we consider the festival bid.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My cross means unavailable. You've blocked the hall, not booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, keeping it from anyone else. Leave it blocked until we've talked to the committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One day. I'll tell them the hold expires tomorrow unless we submit a bid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them our festival has a one-day hold. Once they expect a bid tomorrow, we can spend tonight finishing it.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when I put my spare key under the pot, just as you did? You told me not to clutter the doorstep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was for the plumber to collect. It wasn't meant to stay there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, ready for whoever needs it. Is your front-door key in your bag?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. It's inside, and the door's locked. Yours is still under the pot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you lift it, say whose clutter gets us in. The plumber didn't leave us a spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cross of tape I copied from yours is still on the curtain. You called it untidy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine marked where a chair goes on the floor. Yours is stuck across a torn seam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, marking the weak point. Leave it until the finale's over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seam's split farther. Your tape is the only thing holding the two halves together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then thank the person who left the untidy cross there. Say that before you ask me to peel it off.
